feeds.title: Medievalists.net
feeds.description: Medievalists.net was founded by Sandra Alvarez and Peter Konieczny. We wanted to create something that was vibrant, that changed every day, and that engaged people with the past. We aim to be the first place people go to when they want to learn about the Middle Ages and offer readers news, articles, videos and more about the medieval world and how that history is presented today.

feeds.title: Going Medieval
feeds.description: Going Medieval is a project aimed at making medieval history accessible and entertaining for non-expert audiences.My name is Eleanor Janega. And for my sins, I am a medieval historian. More specifically, I specialist in late medieval sexuality, apocalyptic thought, propaganda, and the urban experience in general, and in central Europe more particularly.

feeds.title: Medieval Histories
feeds.description: Medieval Histories brings you the news about current exhibitions, medieval history, new books, archaeology and research about the Middle Ages.

feeds.title: The History Blog » Medieval
feeds.description: My name is Livius. My interests are primarily European ancient and medieval. I also intend to make a note of all the topically relevant books I read, and a list of all the topically relevant books sitting in a pile glaring at me. Read more on medieval history.

feeds.title: A Corner of Tenth-Century Europe
feeds.description: This blog contains occasional musings, by me, Jonathan Jarrett, M. A. (Cantab.), Ph. D. (Lond.), for whatever may be occupying my mind on matters medieval and so forth which is usually early medievalist thoughts and ponderings. I am a lecturer in medieval history and like to talk and write about it passionately.

feeds.title: Matthias Castle Blog
feeds.description: Matthias Castle Blog covers articles on medieval magic, Ars Notoria, divination, occultism, necromancy, Latin, alternative Christianity, Western esotericism.

feeds.title: Just History Posts
feeds.description: Just History Posts was started after the author, Gemma Hollman, graduated with her Masters in Medieval History. Just History Posts was a way to share the interesting things she had learnt throughout her studies. This blog explores topics in more depth, covering great people, world wonders, social and political history, and even a war against emus.

feeds.title: Medieval Hungary
feeds.description: This blog is edited by Zsombor Jekely, an art historian from Budapest, Hungary. The primary purpose of this blog is to collect news about the field of medieval art history in Hungary and publish them in English.

feeds.title: Medievally Speaking
feeds.description: Medievally Speaking encourages critical engagement with all investigations of and creative commentary on the continuing process of creating the Middle Ages, mostly with reviews and review essays, but also with interviews.

feeds.title: Medieval Ware Blog
feeds.description: Medieval Ware Blog covers articles on early middle ages, Islamic golden age, high middle ages, medieval history and more. Medieval Ware is an online medieval store, where you can find a handpicked selection of some of the most refined medieval and fantasy items in the world.

feeds.title: Merovingian World
feeds.description: Merovingian World is a blog by James T Palmer on the early middle ages and other things. Blog covers articles on medieval manuscripts, medieval medicine, Carolingian history, English/Irish history, global middle ages and Merovingian history.

feeds.title: Historian on the Edge
feeds.description: Historian on the Edge is where medieval history and radical politics bumble into each other and have an existential crisis.

feeds.title: British Library Blog Medieval Manuscripts
feeds.description: The British Library is home to world-class collections of manuscripts including papyri, medieval illuminated manuscripts and early modern state papers. Our ancient, medieval and early modern manuscripts blog promotes the work of our curators, who are responsible for these items and thousands more, including medieval historical and literary manuscripts, charters and seals, and early modern manuscripts.
